Valves & instruments · counted from the model

    Range overview

    Grundfos TP · selection at the duty point

    Curves digitised from the Grundfos TP data booklet (50 Hz, 4-pole). The pump is picked as the smallest motor whose full-speed curve reaches the duty with margin; the VFD then runs it at the speed where the curve passes through the duty point. Orange: system curve. Solid: full speed. Dashed: speed at duty.

    Package weight · shipping and operating

    Breakdown

    Budget weights for transport and structural planning. Shipping = dry, as lifted. Operating = with water in the chiller, plate HX, pumps, piping and cooling tower basin. Piping and water volumes are summed from the pipe runs in the model. Chiller and cooling tower weights to be replaced by Kirloskar and ACTPL data. The 40 ft HC and 20 ft containers are limited to 30.48 t gross.

    Drawings

    Generated from the current selection. GA drawings are drawn from the 3D model with dimensions, weights and the estimated centre of gravity. All drawings are included in both submittals.

    PPR piping · BQ-Rohrsysteme (Germany)

    Quantities taken off the pipe runs in the model. Chilled and condenser water in PP-R Climate Pipe PN 16 (fibre composite, SDR 11, made for chilled water); pipe on the cooling tower framework and outdoors in the UV-protected version. Sizes picked for ≤ 2.4 m/s on the PPR inner diameter. Pipes come in 4 m lengths; 10% cut allowance added.

    Fittings

    Pipe supports · Al Rawabi detail

    Floor stand: 150 × 150 × 10 base plate, telescopic post (Ø62 / Ø50, adjustable 810–990 mm to the saddle), U-saddle and split clamp around the insulated pipe. Elbow support: the same post with a curved 8 mm gusset plate under the bend. Pipes higher up hang from the roof on threaded rods with the same clamp. Spacing from the BQ table for fibre composite pipe (chilled water at 20 °C wall, condenser water at 40 °C).

    The Excel workbook covers the whole plant (equipment, piping, valves and instruments, electrical, controls, structure, logistics and services) with quantities, makes and blank unit-price cells for costing and for sending out as an RFQ.

    Pump head · calculated from the model

    Index circuit per pump, pipe lengths and fittings taken off the 3D runs. Friction by Darcy–Weisbach / Colebrook on the PPR inner diameter (roughness 0.007 mm). Fitting ζ from the BQ resistance table; valves and strainers from typical manufacturer values; equipment pressure drops are allowances to be replaced by Kirloskar, ACTPL and the PHE supplier.

    General arrangement

    Shipping

    Each module ships as a standard container unit. On the cooling tower framework the platforms fold up against the casing, the handrails lie down, and the fan stacks, fans and guards come off and travel loose. Shipping in the view bar shows the plant in this condition.

    Loose items

    I/O list · CSM panel

    Hard-wired points to the CSM controller plus the points read over the network (BACnet / Modbus) from the chiller, drives, ultrasonic flow meter, energy meter and ECOMAX. Spares of 20% are added per card type.

    Annual energy · MCP vs air-cooled plant

    P&ID · standard symbols (Al Rawabi 1.3_P&ID_R01)

    Drawn with the legend and line conventions of 1.3_P&ID_R01 (Al Rawabi Dairy): full pump trains (BFV, NRV, PG, RB, DPS, DV), strainers, instruments, expansion and make-up. Updates with every selection.

    Electrical & control room

    The main incomer and the pump VFD panel stand on the end wall of the 40 ft base module; the CSM panel with the operator HMI stands on the rear wall, beside the personnel door. Turn on Explode to slide the panels out and see the room layout, or use the Control room view.

    Danfoss VLT® AutomationDrive FC 302

    380–500 V (T5), IP20 drives built into the VFD panel, RFI filter H2, 50 °C ambient without derating, efficiency 98% from 11 kW. Frame sizes and dimensions from the Danfoss FC 301/302 selection guide; confirm in Danfoss MyDrive Select for the final motor data.

    Cable trays

    As the Al Rawabi design deck: a power tray (250 × 50) and a control tray (150 × 50) run side by side under the roof of the base module, from the panels to the far end, with drops to local isolators beside every pump, the chiller starter and the field junction boxes. A vertical riser at the electrical end carries both to the cooling tower framework (fan motors, CT pumps on the deck, ECOMAX CT); branches cross into the side module for the secondary pumps and, from 500 TR, the CT pumps.

    Honeywell Forge · remote monitoring

    The CSM panel collects the plant data (chiller, pumps, VFDs, CT fans, ECOMAX, energy meters, sensors). An edge gateway in the CSM panel pushes it to the Honeywell Forge cloud over an outbound, encrypted connection; dashboards, alarms and predictive maintenance run there and are reached from a browser or phone.

    Points pulled from the CSM

    Indicative dashboard with values from this selection at design load. Point list, protocols (BACnet/IP, Modbus TCP from the chiller and VFDs) and cybersecurity scope to be confirmed with Honeywell.

          What ACTPL should rate each model at

          • Thermal design point: WBT 31.5 °C, 40 → 35 °C. Range 5.0 K, approach 3.5 K.
          • Check case, maximum dry bulb: DBT 45.3 °C with WBT 23.9 °C. Thermally easy, but it sets the ambient for fan motors, EC electronics and VFDs, plus evaporation and make-up.
          • Heat rejection includes the compressor heat: chiller TR × (1 + kW/TR ÷ 3.517). At 0.70 kW/TR a 300 TR chiller needs about 360 TR of tower.
          • All electrical and electronic parts rated for 50 °C ambient in direct sun.

          Cooling tower per chiller size · at kW/TR

          Budget figures for structural pre-design, to be replaced by ACTPL data. Tower duty = chiller TR × (1 + kW/TR ÷ 3.517); flow at 5 K range. Shipping = tower dry weight with folded platforms and fans; module adds 3.5 t for the 40 ft HC framework. Operating adds basin water at 300 mm and water in circulation; flooded adds 150 mm to overflow; dynamic adds 50% impact on the fan assemblies. Water loading above 20 m³/h·m² is marked amber.

          Height budget inside the framework

          Construction & materials

          • Casing & basin: FRP, UV-stabilised, fire-retardant resin, flame spread index < 25 (ASTM E84). Basin with sump, strainer, overflow, drain, make-up and equaliser connections. Basin drain and overflow are piped down the module to a gully at grade.
          • Internal structure: pultruded FRP, or hot-dip galvanised / SS316 steel as an option. SS fasteners throughout.
          • Fill: Brentwood, fouling-resistant type selected for the water quality and sand load.
          • Air intake louvers: Brentwood cellular louvers on both long faces.
          • Drift eliminators: Brentwood cellular, drift ≤ 0.001% of circulating flow. The visible plume is warm saturated air leaving the fan stacks.
          • Distribution: engineered low-pressure nozzles for even wetting.
          • Fans: aerofoil FRP, balanced to ISO G 6.3, removable fan stacks with guards. EC fans, or PM direct-drive motors (IE4 minimum) with VFDs.
          • Connections: flanged PN10 at the pump-deck end (60% bay, up to 400 TR) or at the electrical end above the CT pump section (full frame, from 500 TR).
          • Water treatment: ECOMAX CT electrolytic treatment on a side stream (optional), removing hardness as scale on its cathodes and limiting blowdown, with no dosing chemicals.

          Platforms & access

          • Two levels, 600 mm wide, along both long faces: basin level (+650 above the framework base) and spray nozzle level (+2,250). Decks fold up within the 2,896 mm envelope for shipping.
          • Lay-down handrails (1,100 mm, with mid rail and toe board) collapse onto the deck first. ISO corner castings stay clear for lifting and lashing.
          • Access doors to the fill, nozzle and drift eliminator zones from the platforms. Fans serviced from the fan deck with stacks removed.
          • Access ladder on the base module front at the electrical end, shipped loose.

          Fan control

          • Ambient DBT and RH sensor; the CSM calculates the wet bulb.
          • Cold water set point = ambient WBT + design approach, never below the chiller's minimum condenser entering temperature (Kirloskar to advise).
          • All fans run together at the same speed (EC or VFD), which gives the lowest fan power at part load.
          • Fan speed, status, alarms and kWh to the CSM over Modbus or BACnet, and on to Honeywell Forge.

          Build, test and ship

          1. Framework fabricatedThe 40 ft HC framework is built to the MCP drawings and sent to ACTPL.
          2. Assembly at Killa PardiACTPL assembles the complete tower inside the framework: casing, fill, nozzles, drift eliminators, fans and drives, platforms folded.
          3. Ship assembled to RajewadiThe assembled module goes to Kirloskar Chillers, Rajewadi, within the 40 ft HC envelope.
          4. Factory test with the MCPThe tower module is mounted on the base module and run with the chiller plant: hydraulic, controls and fan tests, AHRI-witnessed chiller test. Thermal rating backed by ACTPL's test rig and confirmed on site per CTI ATC-105.
          5. Ship to siteShipped as standard 40 ft HC / 20 ft units within 30.48 t each (see Weights); platforms unfolded and fan stacks fitted on site.
